newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cabinet agrees to speed up highway projects.
newsitem.headline: Czech cabinet agrees to speed up highway projects.

text.p: The Czech government on Wednesday agreed to speed up spending on new motorway construction, with a plan to build a new 458 km highway costing 120 billion crowns through the year 2002, Transport Minister Martin Riman said.

Speaking after a cabinet meeting, Riman said that 105 billion crowns would be paid through the state budget, and that about 15 billion crowns should come from a credit granted by a foreign institution.
He said that the foreign lending institution had yet to be determined as well as the timing for the drawing of the credit.
According to the government's previous plan, about 370 km of highway and motorway was to have been built by the year 2002.
The new plan would increase the total length of the Czech network to 1,222 km, with an additional 300 km to be built between 2002 and 2005.
The total costs through the year 2005 are forecast at 190 billion crowns, Riman said.
